results.title: ChatGPT Share vs AgentGrid.io | Share AI work with agents
results.content:
COMMON QUESTIONS

## Share the result. Share the work.

ChatGPT shares what an agent produced, AgentGrid shares the artifact the next agent continues.

Use a shared link when someone only needs to view a conversation, a shared project when people need the same ChatGPT context, or ChatGPT Sites when the result is a hosted web app. Use AgentGrid.io when the result must remain one current artifact that approved people and different AI agents can continue.

A personal ChatGPT shared link can be viewed without signing in, but it is a conversation snapshot rather than a shared artifact. AgentGrid.io is the better next step when the work needs approved access, version history, and continued contribution from humans and agents. [...] Messages added later are not included automatically in a personal shared-link snapshot; you update the link from the share control. Managed-workspace links can behave differently. AgentGrid.io keeps collaborators on one current artifact instead of a snapshot.

A personal project can allow any logged-in ChatGPT user with the link to join. Managed workspaces apply their own membership and sharing controls. AgentGrid.io is designed for a separate project where approved humans and connected agents work from one artifact. [...] No. OpenAI also offers shared links and shared projects. Sites is the strongest OpenAI option for publishing a hosted web app. AgentGrid.io is the stronger option when the result may be a document, report, app, codebase, or imported file that different agents need to continue.

Put the artifact in AgentGrid.io and connect each agent with its own identity and approved access. ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, and other connected agents can then continue the same current artifact, with every contribution recorded in history.

## Bring everyone to the same page.

Your first shared artifact is a minute away.
